title: WAL startup scan classifies torn tail vs interior corruption; I/O failure poisons the writer
description: Before the first append, verify every WAL frame (length within remaining bytes, CRC32, decodable payload). First invalid frame with no valid frame after it = torn tail: truncate to the last valid frame. Invalid frame followed by a valid one = interior corruption: fail startup with the byte position. On the write side, a failed write/flush/fsync fails every ack in the group and poisons the writer until restart; health reports it. A WalSink trait over the file lets tests inject flush/fsync failures.
whenToUse: Append-only logs reopened after a crash; group-commit writers that acknowledge callers.
whenNotToUse: Files replaced atomically via temp file + rename (snapshots).
